sections.body:
A fruit is the part of a plant that holds its seeds. Trees, bushes and vines all grow fruits. Some fruits are very big, like a watermelon. Some are very small, like a grape.

Fruits like warm days and soft rain. A mango tree in the south of Vietnam gives fruit in summer. An apple tree in Europe gives fruit in autumn. The season tells us when a fruit is sweetest.

Every fruit has parts. The outside skin is the **peel**. Inside, the fruit is soft and juicy. That part is called the **flesh**. In the middle there are **seeds**. Some fruits have one big seed. A peach has a hard stone. Some fruits have many tiny seeds, like a strawberry.

Fruit is good for your body. It has water, so it helps you feel fresh on a hot day. It has **vitamins**, which are tiny helpers that keep you well. It has fibre, which helps your tummy work every day.

Some fruit is nice to eat raw. An apple is lovely raw. Some fruit is nicer after cooking. A banana is good cooked, and so is a green mango in a curry.

And fruit is a happy food to share. You can cut a melon into pieces and put it on the table for everybody.
examples: This is a mango. It is a fruit.
The seeds are inside the peach.
sections.heading: What is a fruit?

sections.body:
Bananas grow in bunches on tall plants. They are green first and yellow when they are ripe. A banana gives your body energy very quickly.

Mangoes are called the king of fruits in Vietnam. They can be green, yellow or red. The Nam Dok Mai of the south is small and very sweet.

Apples are crisp and sweet. One small apple has about 80 calories in it.

Oranges are full of vitamin C. You can eat them in slices or squeeze them for juice.

Watermelon is almost all water. It is red inside, and its black seeds are in the middle. In summer, many Vietnamese families buy one on the road.

Grapes come in green and purple. They grow in bunches, and each one is small and sweet.

Pineapple is spiky on the outside and yellow inside. It is called a pineapple because of its shape, like a pine cone.

Papaya grows tall and straight. Its orange flesh is soft, and you can eat it with a spoon.

Every fruit was once a small flower on a tree. Bees carried the pollen from flower to flower. Then the fruit grew, and the seeds grew inside it.
examples: This orange is full of vitamin C.
We cut the watermelon on the step.
sections.heading: Fruits we know and where they grow

sections.body:
Fruit comes from outside, so it carries dust. A little water and clean hands keep you safe.

First, wash your hands with soap. Then wash the fruit under running water. Do not soak it for a long time.

Next, put the fruit on a clean plate or board. Use a clean knife, and cut it away from your body.

Then cut it in the right way. Cut round fruit in half first, then cut each half. Cut a long fruit, like a banana or a mango, into slices from the top down.

Look at the fruit before you eat it. Throw away any part that is brown, soft or smells strange.

And finally, eat slowly and sit down. Your body likes fruit better when you are calm.
examples: I wash my hands before I cut the mango.
The apple is under the tap now.
I cut the banana from the top down.
sections.heading: How to wash and cut a fruit
steps: Wash the fruit under running water.
Put it on a clean board and use a clean knife.
Cut round fruit in half, then in slices.
Check the fruit and throw away any bad part.

sections.body:
These are the words that grown-ups use for fruit. Once you know them, you can describe any fruit you see.

A **fruit** is a plant part that holds seeds and is good to eat. **Fruit** is the big word. A mango and a pear are both fruit.

A **seed** is the small hard thing inside a fruit. Plant it in soil and a new plant can grow. An apple seed, or a mango seed, can grow into a tree.

A fruit is **ripe** when it is sweet and ready to eat. A green mango is not ripe yet. A yellow banana is ripe.

The **peel** is the outside skin of a fruit. You usually do not eat it. But you can eat an orange peel, and it makes a good drink.

A **vitamin** is a tiny helper inside food that keeps your body working well. Fruit has plenty of them. One orange gives you a big share of the vitamin C you need each day.
examples: This fruit is not ripe yet.
Peel the banana before you eat it.
Fruit has vitamins that keep us well.
sections.heading: The words we use for fruit

terms.example: A mango and a pear are both fruit.
terms.gloss: A part of a plant that holds seeds and is good to eat, like a mango or a pear.

terms.example: I planted the mango seed in a pot.
terms.gloss: The small hard part inside a fruit. Plant it in soil and a new plant can grow.

terms.example: This banana is yellow and ripe.
terms.gloss: Ready to eat, sweet and soft. A green mango is not ripe yet.

terms.example: I peel the orange before I eat it.
terms.gloss: The outside skin of a fruit. You usually peel it before eating.

terms.example: One orange gives me lots of vitamin C.
terms.gloss: A tiny helper in food that keeps your body working well. Fruit has plenty of vitamins.

sections.body:
Most fruit is safe for everybody. But a few fruits are not.

If you have a **nut allergy**, some fruits share the same nuts inside them. A mango seed can give you the same reaction as a nut. If a fruit makes your mouth itchy or your skin itchy, stop eating it and tell an adult.

Small round fruit can go down the wrong way. Grapes, cherries and hard nuts are the ones that get stuck most often. Cut grapes in half, and always sit down when you eat them.

Never eat a fruit that fell on the road, or one that is soft and brown inside. When in doubt, ask an adult.

And one more rule: wash fruit every time. Even the fruit you peel. Dirt on the outside can get on your hands and then on your mouth.
examples: I cut the grapes in half.
This fruit makes my mouth itchy, so I will not eat it.
We always wash fruit before we eat it.
sections.heading: Some fruit can make you ill

sections.body:
Fruit is not a treat. It is part of a good day.

Fruit gives you **water**. On a hot afternoon in Hanoi, a cold slice of watermelon is better than a sweet drink. Your body uses the water straight away.

Fruit gives you **vitamins**. Your body needs them to grow tall, to heal a cut, and to keep away illness. Orange, mango and guava are full of vitamin C. Carrots are a vegetable, but they help your eyes too.

Fruit gives you **fibre**. Your tummy pushes the food along. Fruit with the skin on has more fibre than fruit without it.

Fruit also gives you **energy**. A banana before a game is a good idea. So is a handful of grapes.

Try this simple idea. Keep one fruit in your bag. When you feel hungry in the afternoon, eat that first. Then see how you feel afterwards.

You do not have to eat a lot of fruit. Three small pieces each day is a fine amount. And you should try many kinds. A week of only one fruit is a boring week for your body.
examples: I keep a banana in my school bag.
Fruit gives me water and vitamins.
I eat fruit before I play outside.
sections.heading: Why fruit is good for you every day

item.summary: A fruit is a plant part that holds seeds. After reading this you can name the parts of a fruit, tell your friends where your fruit comes from, and wash and cut fruit safely at home.
item.title: Let's Learn About Fruits
